title: Compliance Administrator - Leading Recruitment Company
description:
Join Prospero Teaching - Where Passion Meets Purpose in Education!

For over 20 years, Prospero Teaching has been a trusted leader in connecting teaching and support staff with schools, academies, and nurseries across the UK and internationally. We proudly offer our services to a broad range of educational settings, including EYFS, Primary, Secondary, Further Education, SEN, and PRUs.

About the Role

As a Compliance Administrator, you will be a key member of our compliance team, responsible for ensuring candidates meet the necessary regulatory and internal requirements to work within the education sector. You will play a vital role in maintaining compliance with industry standards and fostering a smooth recruitment process for candidates.

Key Responsibilities
- Collaborate with the compliance team to ensure candidates meet all compliance standards for the education sector.
- Follow established operational processes and procedures to ensure adherence to regulations and industry standards.
- Guide and support candidates throughout the recruitment process.
- Conduct compliance checks, including but not limited to right-to-work, DBS, reference, and employment history verifications.
- Maintain and update accurate candidate records.
- Organise and verify candidate documentation.
- Respond to both internal and external inquiries efficiently and professionally.

About You

We are looking for a motivated and detail-oriented individual with:
- A good general education (minimum GCSEs in Maths and English, grades A-C, or equivalent).
- Strong relationship-building skills.
- The ability to work effectively under deadlines.
- Excellent administrative and organizational abilities, with a talent for prioritizing tasks.
- Strong communication and customer service skills.
- An understanding of confidentiality and data protection.
- A proactive problem-solving mindset.
- A commitment to safeguarding practices.

Benefits
- Competitive salary with a commission structure.
- Ongoing training and opportunities for professional development.
- Clear career advancement prospects within the company.
- A dynamic and collaborative work environment.
- Private healthcare.
- Quarterly performance-based incentives.

Join us and be part of a team that's helping drive one of the UK's fastest-growing recruitment firms forward.

title: ER Officer (Advisor)
description:
A large, values-led organisation currently recruiting an Employee Relations Officer on a fixed-term basis initially. Joining a well-established People team, you will work alongside a dedicated Employee Relations function. This opportunity would suit a HR professional who enjoys managing employee relations casework, building strong relationships with managers and delivering a high-quality people service.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone looking to further develop their employee relations expertise within a supportive and collaborative environment, where learning and development is actively encouraged.

Immediate start available.

The Role

As Employee Relations Officer, you will be responsible for managing a range of employee relations matters and supporting managers across the organisation with practical, timely guidance.
Your responsibilities will include:
- Managing lower level employee relations cases from initial enquiry through to conclusion.
- Providing advice and support on absence management, disciplinary, grievance and performance-related matters.
- Triaging employee relations queries through a central case management system and ensuring cases are allocated appropriately.
- Coordinating and processing occupational health referrals and supporting managers with recommendations and outcomes.
- Advising managers on policies, procedures and best-practice approaches to people management.
- Supporting investigations, meetings and hearings relating to employee relations matters.
- Maintaining accurate documentation and case records in line with policy and data protection requirements.
- Escalating more complex cases to the senior Employee Relations team where required.
- Contributing to continuous improvement initiatives that enhance the employee experience and service delivery.

About You

We are keen to speak with candidates who have a solid HR foundation and previous experience supporting employee relations activity. You will ideally bring:
- Experience handling employee relations casework across areas such as absence, performance, disciplinary and grievance. (ESSENTIAL)
- Strong communication skills, with the confidence to support managers through sensitive conversations.
- Excellent organisational skills and the ability to manage a varied caseload.
- A customer-focused and proactive approach to problem-solving.
- Knowledge of employment legislation and HR best practice.
- Experience working within a large or complex organisation would be advantageous.

CIPD qualification, or progress towards one, would be beneficial, although relevant practical experience will also be considered.

Candidates who have managed absence, grievance, disciplinary and performance cases from start to finish will be of particular interest, although experience managing every stage of a formal disciplinary process is not essential.

What's on Offer
- Pension: Enhanced employer contribution.
- Holiday: 25 days + bank holidays + Christmas shutdown (24 Dec - 5 Jan)
- Flexible Working: 3 days on-site, 2 remote.
- 35 hour working week.
- Extras: Benefits platforms, student discounts plus others.
- Potential for further opportunity and development within the wider organisation.
- Exposure to a broad range of HR casework and stakeholder groups.

What you need to do now:
If you're interested in this role, click 'apply now' to forward an up-to-date copy of your CV, or call us now.
If this job isn't quite right for you, but you are looking for a new position, please contact us for a confidential discussion about your career.

title: HR Administrator
description:
HR Administrator

Location: Disley, Cheshire
Salary: 28,000 - 30,000 per annum
Job Type: Permanent, Full Time
Environment: Industrial / Manufacturing

The Role

We are seeking a highly organised and proactive HR Administrator / Site Administrator to join our busy manufacturing site in Disley. This is a varied role combining HR administration, general office support, and assistance with day-to-day site management activities.

Working closely with the Site Leadership Team, you will play a key part in ensuring the smooth running of administrative and HR processes while providing excellent support to employees, visitors, and management.

Key Responsibilities
HR Administration
- Maintain accurate employee records and personnel files.
- Support recruitment activities including advertising vacancies, arranging interviews, and onboarding new starters.
- Prepare contracts, offer letters, and employee documentation.
- Record and monitor absence, holiday, and sickness information.
- Assist with disciplinary, grievance, and performance management administration.
- Support training administration and maintain training records.
- Process HR-related paperwork and ensure compliance with company procedures.

Site & Office Administration
- Provide general administrative support to the site management team.
- Manage incoming calls, emails, and correspondence.
- Organise meetings
- Maintain office supplies and liaise with suppliers.
- Assist with visitor management and site inductions.
- Support health & safety administration and document control.
- Produce reports, spreadsheets, and site KPI information
- Ensure filing systems are maintained accurately and confidentially.

Office Manager Support Duties
- Assist with the day-to-day running of the office environment.
- Coordinate facilities-related activities and contractor visits.
- Support site communications and employee notices.
- Help organise company events, meetings, and employee engagement initiatives.
- Monitor and manage office equipment and resources.
- Provide additional support for operational projects as required.

About You

We are looking for someone who:
- Has previous experience within an HR, Administrative, Site Administration, or Office Management support role.
- Is confident using Microsoft Office, particularly Word, Excel, and Outlook.
- Has excellent organisational skills and attention to detail.
- Can handle confidential information professionally.
- Possesses strong communication and interpersonal skills.
- Is able to prioritise a varied workload in a fast-paced industrial environment.
- Has experience within manufacturing, industrial, engineering, or production environments (desirable but not essential).

Benefits
- Competitive salary of 28,000 - 30,000 per annum
- Permanent, full-time position
- Excellent benefits package
- Company pension scheme
- Life assurance
- Health & wellbeing support
- Employee assistance programme
- Training and development opportunities
- Career progression opportunities
- Employee discounts
- Free on-site parking
- Generous holiday entitlement

If you are a motivated administrator looking for a varied role within a busy industrial environment, we would love to hear from you.

Adecco acts as an employment agency for permanent recruitment and an employment business for the supply of temporary workers. The Adecco Group UK & Ireland is an Equal Opportunities Employer.

By applying for this role your details will be submitted to Adecco. Our Candidate Privacy Information Statement explaining how we will use your information is available on our website.

title: Human Resources & Recruitment Assistant
People and Data Administrator
description:
People & Data Administrator Full-Time Hybrid Manchester

Join Spire Healthcare as a People & Data Administrator and help drive data accuracy, system excellence, and informed decision-making across our People function.

We're looking for a detail-oriented and analytical professional to support the administration of our people systems, reporting processes, and data management activities. This is an exciting opportunity for someone with experience in HR systems, people data, or HR administration who enjoys working with data and technology to improve business processes.

About the Role

As a People & Data Administrator, you'll play a key role in supporting the integrity, security, and effective use of people data across the organisation. Working closely with People, IT, and business stakeholders, you'll help maintain our Oracle HCM system, produce meaningful reports, support system upgrades and testing, and contribute to continuous improvement initiatives.

Key Responsibilities
- Support the administration and maintenance of Oracle HCM and related people systems.
- Produce regular and ad hoc people reports and data insights.
- Conduct data audits, identify discrepancies, and support data cleansing activities.
- Manage user access and permissions whilst ensuring compliance with data protection requirements.
- Support system testing, upgrades, enhancements, and user acceptance testing.
- Provide second-line support for people systems queries.
Identify opportunities to improve processes, reporting, and system efficiency.

What We're Looking For
- Experience in HR Systems, HR Administration, HRIS, or People Data roles.
- Experience using Oracle HCM or a similar HR system.
- Strong Microsoft Excel skills, including Pivot Tables, lookups, and data analysis.
- Experience producing reports and analysing data.
- Knowledge of HR processes and employee lifecycle management.
- Understanding of GDPR, data governance, and information security principles.
- Excellent attention to detail, problem-solving skills, and ability to manage confidential information.
- Power BI experience is desirable.

Why Join Spire Healthcare?

At Spire Healthcare, our people make the difference. You'll be joining a supportive team where continuous improvement, collaboration, and professional development are encouraged.

Our values guide everything we do:
- Caring is our passion
- Driving clinical excellence
- Doing the right thing
- Keeping it simple
- Delivering on our promises
- Succeeding and celebrating together

About Us

Spire Healthcare is a leading independent healthcare group in the United Kingdom, running 38 hospitals and over 50 clinics across England, Wales and Scotland. It provides diagnostics, inpatient, day case and outpatient care, operates a network of private GPs and provides workplace health services to over 800 corporate clients. It also delivers a range of private and NHS mental health, musculoskeletal and dermatological services.

We have achieved our market leading position because of our Purpose, which is to 'make a positive difference to people's lives through outstanding personalised care'. Everyone at Spire is aligned to this purpose, which underpins a culture of respect, inclusion, passion and collaboration across our business, enabling us to achieve more than 98% of our hospitals being rated 'Good' or 'Outstanding' by the Regulators; these are sector leading standards.

title: Recruitment Administrator
description:
This Recruitment Administrator role in Manchester is all about keeping the hiring process running smoothly. You'll be handling the essential day-to-day tasks that make recruitment operations efficient and successful.

Client Details

This organisation operates within the business services sector and is based in Manchester.

Description
- Coordinate and schedule interviews, ensuring all parties are informed and prepared.
- Manage candidate records and ensure databases are up to date and accurate.
- Support the recruitment team by preparing job descriptions and posting job advertisements.
- Communicate with candidates, providing updates and responding to queries promptly.
- Assist with onboarding processes and documentation for new hires.
- Maintain compliance with company policies and employment regulations.
- Generate recruitment reports and provide administrative support to the HR team.
- Collaborate with team members to improve recruitment processes.
- Supporting candidates payroll.

Profile

A successful Recruitment Administrator should have:
- Strong organisational skills and attention to detail.
- Experience in a recruitment or administrative role within the business services sector.
- Good communication skills, both written and verbal.
- Proficiency in using recruitment systems or HR software.
- A proactive approach to problem-solving and multitasking.

Job Offer
- Salary ranging from 25,000+, dependent on the level of experience.
- Permanent position with opportunities to grow within the company.
- Standard holiday allowance and other company benefits.

If you're interested in this role, apply now.

title: Recruitment Team Manager
description:
Recruitment Team Manager - Manchester

40k plus per annum (DOE) + Commission, Rewards, Benefits & Incentives

Daniel Owen has been the leading name in the construction recruitment industry for over 40 years, growing in size, sectors and expertise throughout that time. We are still continuing to grow and part of this growth is the expansion of the team in our Manchester office where we are looking for an experienced Recruitment Manager to join us.

This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced recruitment professional to lead and shape a team of experienced Construction & Facilities Management recruiters within a nationally respected business. Backed by our strong reputation in the construction sector and a truly supportive, people-first culture, this is a chance to put your name on the map and lead a high performing team to further success.

Your impact/duties as a Recruitment Team Manager:
- Client Relationships: Not just over the phone, but face-to-face, you'll identify and develop existing and new client relationships.
- Top-Tier Service: Deliver exceptional service to ensure repeat business and outstanding recommendations, taking a hands on approach to recruitment, candidate sourcing and client requirements
- Leadership & Team Building: Be able to lead the development of an established team, providing hands on leadership and coaching to members of staff
- Talent Development: Identify strengths and development areas within the team, supporting career progression and helping to build the next generation of recruitment leaders
- Strategy & Development: Work closely with the management team to develop and implement strategies that support the continued growth of the Manchester office and wider business
- Brand Growth: Be the face of Daniel Owen in the Manchester area, promoting the brand with professionalism and integrity

The Ideal Candidate for a Recruitment Team Manager:
- Proven Professional: Proven experience in construction recruitment with a strong understanding of the industry and a track record of billing success
- Leadership Experience: Managerial qualities allowing you to build, manage and develop a high performing team around you
- Excellent Communicator: Posses brilliant communication skills face-to-face and via email to allow for new clients and business growth
- Motivator and Ambitious: Inspire others and aspire to progress into a Senior Managerial level role
- Decision-Maker: You're not afraid to take the initiative and adapt to fast changing priorities

Extra benefits of working as a Recruitment Team Manager at Daniel Owen:
- Top Tier Holiday Allowance:Increasing holiday allowance for the first five years, reaching 28 days, plus your birthday off and an additional day for charitable endeavours.
- Health and Wellbeing:Private healthcare through Vitality, contributory pension and life assurance.
- Director Incentives:Quarterly lunch incentives and personal treat vouchers.
- Loyalty Rewards:Additional holiday entitlement and bonus payments linked to service milestones.
- Annual Reward Trips:Multiple company trips throughout the year, with previous destinations including Marbella, Prague and Portugal.
- Learning and Growth:Access to the Daniel Owen Academy, featuring a structured 12-week training programme alongside one-to-one coaching and ongoing development.
- Financial Wellbeing Support:Access to professional financial guidance through our partnership with One Financial.
- Fast-Track Career Development:Our directors all climbed the ladder from within making progression visible and achievable.

If you envision a future where you're evolving, and making a significant impact within our dynamic team, don't hesitate - Apply directly or connect with our Talent Acquisition Team for a confidential conversation.
